sermon.title: Idolatry and Idols Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues 1 Corinthians 10, teaching that the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils cannot be shared and that churches cannot be built on human opinions. He gives Paul’s practical advice about meat sold in the market and offered to idols, then turns to Acts 15:29, greed as idolatry, and the works of the flesh. He closes by arguing from James 2 and Revelation 2 that believers should not say “my faith” but follow the faith of Jesus.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “James chapter 18” for the passage on showing your faith by your works (James 2:18), and “Revelation 2:12” for the words “you have not denied My faith,” which are in Revelation 2:13 (verse 12 begins the letter to Pergamos); his words are unchanged and both passages are shown. Several names (ministers, public figures and candidates) were spelled from the captions and some are marked [unclear]; he makes strong claims about named people, groups and political parties, which are his words, not verified by this site. He also makes a health remark about drinking blood and mentions Pentecost (Pentecostal) churches and Catholic practices critically. Where he reads Scripture aloud he often uses King James wording.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to sacrifice to devils and create your own religion? (Leviticus 17:7)
chunks.short_answer: He says it is “Old Testament stuff”: they sacrificed “to devils, not to God, to gods whom they knew not.” He says “they created their own religion. And when you create your own religion, you’re going the way of Satan,” and he cites Leviticus 17:7, “They shall no more offer their sacrifices unto” devils.
chunks.text: Well, what do you mean, to sacrifice to the devils? Well, it’s Old Testament stuff, basic. People know this that read their Bible. They sacrificed to devils, not to God, to gods whom they knew not. To knew God, they created their own religion. And when you create your own religion, you’re going the way of Satan. See, he loves for you to alter the one true God and the Bible that tells us how to get there. He’s just quoting Old Testament Scripture, Leviticus 17:7: “They shall no more offer their sacrifices unto” what? Devils. To idols, their own.

chunks.section_question: Can you drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils? (1 Corinthians 10:21-22)
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul’s point is “they’re not compatible.” Using your human understanding that an idol is nothing to “violate the direct commandments of God and provoke God to jealousy” is, he says, saying “we are God”: “You don’t come out and say it, you just do it with your beliefs, from your human thinking.”
chunks.text: Religion isn’t that good. Hallelujah. Verse 21, still in 1 Corinthians chapter 10:21: “You can’t drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils, nor be partakers of the Lord’s table and of the table of devils.” They’re not compatible. “Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?” Because you got some human understanding that an idol is nothing and the meat sacrificed to the idol is nothing, do you use that understanding to violate the direct commandments of God and provoke God to jealousy? Are you stronger than God? Have you become a God? And when we do our own religious ways, come up with our own way of serving God--

chunks.section_question: Can you build a healthy church on human opinions or denominations?
chunks.short_answer: He says “you can’t build a healthy church and violate God’s Word,” and “it must be Jesus, His truth, His words, and the apostles’ doctrine.” He says “being a Baptist has nothing to do with anything. Being a Catholic has nothing to do with anything,” and that Paul gives a practical solution next “because Christians get weird.”
chunks.text:
Amen. Conclusion of this approach, the spiritual approach, the spiritual illustration: do not partake of idols nor food sacrificed to idols. His conclusion was the same in both approaches. I like this guy, Paul. You can’t build a healthy church and violate God’s Word. You can’t build a healthy church, you’ve been using human understanding. You must have the mind of the Spirit. You cannot build a healthy church using your own opinions and your own beliefs. It must be Jesus, His truth, His words, and the apostles’ doctrine, who got their doctrine straight from Jesus.

So Calvin, Wesley, and all the rest down through, or Roberts, Billy Graham, have nothing to do with anything. I must build my Christianity on Jesus Christ, His words, His truths. Amen. Being a Baptist has nothing to do with anything. Being a Catholic has nothing to do with anything. Verse 25 of chapter 10, 1 Corinthians 10:25: now here’s the practical solution. And why is he bringing out the practical? Because Christians get weird. You know, we read in the Bible, uh, to be modest. Well, then we decide, well, I can’t wear short-sleeve shirts, I can’t wear shorts, I can’t wear jewelry, or, and the Bible says don’t, women, don’t decorate yourself with your hair, don’t fix your hair up, and, and, and outward adorning of makeup and jewelry and all this stuff. You know, Pentecostalism, I grew up in Pentecost churches, and they had spirit writing, “Holy Ghost, come home,” and they’d write something and it made no sense, and all kinds of goony stuff. Just buy the meat, because you already know it means nothing,” and at an unbeliever’s feast eat what is set before you, since over-investigating makes “a miserable life for ourselves.”

You know, don’t be one of these weird Christians: “Is it got the stamp? Is it culture? Is it got the Christian approval on it?” Don’t get--don’t investigate, just buy the stuff and go eat it. chunks.section_question: When should you not eat meat that was offered to idols? (1 Corinthians 10:28-29)
chunks.short_answer: He says if someone tells you it was offered in sacrifice to idols, “don’t eat it, for whose conscience’ sake? His, the one who told you,” so you don’t “offend the conscience of the other one, even the idolater.” He then says that in his youth things like pool were called sin, and “now we’re going to the other thing: everything’s okay, now there is no restraints.”
chunks.text:
“Whose conscience? If any say it’s offered in sacrifice to idols, don’t eat it, for whose conscience’ sake?” His, the one who told you. See, now the cat’s out of the bag, you know, to obey the Scriptures. So you go, you know, “I’ll--I’ll just eat the potatoes and beans today.” Why? Because you don’t want to offend the conscience of the other one, even the idolater who knows you shouldn’t be eating meat sacrificed to his god. That’s why he brought it up. Then you can say, “Well, I didn’t know. I--I won’t have any of that, thank you. Just give me the mashed potatoes and the gravy and the beans, and everything will be fine.” Are you there?

Is this good or what? Oh, this is--see, back in my day you couldn’t even have a deck of cards in your house. Back in my day, my teenage, you could not play billiards, pool. That was sin. Why? Because all the pool tables were in the bars or a pool hall where all the hoods and everybody hung out. So instead of saying the atmosphere was wrong, we--they just said playing pool, “that’s the devil’s game, man, that’s a sin.” And how many, you know, there’s nothing wrong with playing pool. How many, you know, I got a pool table in my garage. See, we got extreme, but now we’re going to the other thing: everything’s okay, now there is no restraints.

For why is my liberty judged by another man’s conscience?

chunks.section_question: What did the Jerusalem church decide about meat offered to idols, blood and things strangled? (Acts 15:29)
chunks.short_answer: He says the apostles, elders and members “unanimously made it clear” in Acts 15:29 to “abstain from meats offered to idols,” and “100% unanimously voted yes.” On blood and things strangled, he says it relates to Christ’s blood sacrifice: “we only eat of His blood in the communion table,” because “the shedding of blood was imperative for the forgiveness of sins in the Bible from the beginning.”
chunks.text:
But isn’t this good? Isn’t this practical? You know, the Bible says in Ecclesiastes, “do not be extreme in anything.” Okay, and so we need to watch out with being extreme. We need to be practical. Now, the apostles, the elders, and the members of the church in Jerusalem unanimously made it clear--unanimously means they were not divided, which was the first topic that he talked about for four chapters, went to division--this church is in unity, and they make it very clear, Acts 15:29: “Abstain, abstain from meats offered to idols.” Is that clear? The apostles, the elders of the church, and the members, 100% unanimously voted yes, this is what we’re to follow.

And these people, with their human thinking, were violating what they had already come up with. Can I hear an amen? Are you there? Through their human thinking. And he says, “from blood and things strangled.” Now, why do you think they said, don’t partake of blood and don’t eat of meat strangled? Because it’s related to Christ’s blood sacrifice for us. The blood had to be shed. You know, you can drink blood and you won’t die from it. You know, blood is a food, and unless it has germs and bacteria and disease in it, you’re not going to catch anything. Okay, a lot of nations and cultures eat blood, blood of cows and so forth. They will cut the vein in the neck of a cow--

Let the blood come out, just shoots out, fill up their cup, then they put pressure on the wound, and in just a few seconds the blood stops flowing. They drink their blood. See, it’s a food, but we don’t do it because of what Christ shed His blood, and so we only eat of His blood in the communion table, and we only partake of the thing that was shedding blood, not strangled, because the shedding of blood was imperative for the forgiveness of sins in the Bible from the beginning. Are you with me? It had nothing to do with being bad. Yes, the shedding of blood in Genesis--

chunks.section_question: Are there Protestant idols, and is greed idolatry? (Colossians 3:5)
chunks.short_answer: He says America is not into images: “they worship things that they should not worship.” Reading Colossians 3:5, he says greed is idolatry, and he criticizes the prosperity message, saying he watched ministers “talk senior citizens into giving their whole Social Security check.” But being rich does not make a person greedy: “the Bible doesn’t back up that at all.”
chunks.text:
Well, they wouldn’t have an image. No Protestant church would have an image. I told you at the beginning that America wasn’t into images, they’re into things. They worship things that they should not worship. Well, show me a Protestant idol. Okay, glad you asked. First Colossians, that shouldn’t be First Colossians, I put that one in there to--never mind. Colossians 3:5: “Mortify, put to death, therefore, your members which are upon the earth”: sexual immorality, that’s one of the topics he talked about, “impurity, lust, evil desires.” That was the source of division. “I want it my way, I want it my way, and if you don’t go my way, I can’t go anywhere with you.” Division, and “greed, which is” what? “Idolatry.”

Oh, greed is idolatry. Ew. Kenyon, Oral Roberts, A. A. Allen, T. L. Osborn, Kenneth Hagin, Jimmy Swaggart, Jim Bakker, Robert Tilton, Benny Hinn, Kenneth Copeland, Creflo Dollar, Eddie Long, Joyce Meyer, Paula White are just the few in the Protestant--

Arena that promote prosperity is what God wants for everyone. The prosperity message is promoted by all of these big men, and who? It’s a Ponzi scheme. You give to Kenneth Copeland, God will bless you; you give the dollar, God will bless you. The Ponzi scheme is: the ones on the top get what? The money, they get the benefit, and the ones down here get nothing. And I watched this as a young Christian in the church world. I watched these ministers talk senior citizens into giving their whole Social Security check, and I knew these senior citizens, I knew they just barely survived and barely lived.

I even went up to them and I says, “You know, that old lady over there sitting beside me dropped in her whole paycheck, her whole Social Security. You know, you--aren’t you going to give that back?” “No way, man.” They had their Rolls-Royce Silver Shadow sitting out there, they had $500 suits. “Nothing is too good for the man of God.” I had to work through this stuff. See, you’re lucky, I’m telling you the truth. You don’t have to figure this stuff out. Greed is what? Idolatry. Now, does it mean because a person is rich that they’re greedy? No, the Bible doesn’t back up that at all. If a person goes to college, learns a good job skill, and they make good money of being a lawyer or doctor or whatever, that’s just the good old capitalistic system, and the system that the Bible--

chunks.section_question: What are “individual idols,” and what are the works of the flesh? (Galatians 5:19-21)
chunks.short_answer: He says individual idols, neither Protestant nor Catholic, are “wrong” according to Paul. In Galatians 5:19 “the works of the flesh are evident. They’re very clear, they’re very plain,” and he says the list, including idolatry, division and quarreling, belongs to “the topic of division that Paul covered”; “you’re carnal, you’re babies when you do this.”
chunks.text:
Promotes. And the sad thing is, these ministers just keep finding new suckers to support them, because they promise some miracles and they promise them, you know, “God’s going to, it’s going to be amazing, people just come, come along and give you money that you wouldn’t even know about,” and it doesn’t happen. Are you there? Now, the Catholic church, I can’t find any of this taught in the Catholic church. It’s Protestant. Hallelujah. Okay, what about individual idols? Individual idols, not Protestant, not Catholic. Well, according to Paul, they’re wrong, although they use human knowledge to clear their conscience. Galatians 5:19: “The works of the flesh are evident.” They’re very clear, they’re very plain. Okay, the bottom line: the works of the flesh will not inherit what? The kingdom of God. So what are the works of the flesh? Well, “adultery, fornication,” what Paul--

Addressed in his seminar on church growth, “uncleanness, envy, lewdness, idolatry,” what Paul is addressing now. Idolatry is a what? Work of the flesh. Idolatry. “Spiritual adultery, sorcery, witchcraft, hatred”: you don’t like a certain race, you don’t like women because they’re women, or men because they’re men, or rich because they’re rich. “Hatred, wrath, contention, selfish ambitions, and dissensions”: quarreling, selfish ambition--do you want it your way?--and division are all in the topic of division that Paul covered. Intoxication. A big thing now is Christians getting drunk. We can get tattoos, no problem, our body is a, uh, what do they call the artist [unclear]? chunks.section_question: Is it biblical to say “my faith”? (James 2:18)
chunks.short_answer: He says candidates in debates say “my faith” like “we can have a choice to believe what we want to,” but “my faith” is “only mentioned twice in the Bible,” and “we don’t have a right to say my faith.” In James he says “what I do is going to show you what I’m persuaded in,” and believing in one God makes you “as good as the demons.”
chunks.text:
[Unclear], Romney all say, and Ron, all say in their debates: “my faith.” They say it like we can have a choice to believe what we want to. Romney says “my faith,” and what he means is he’s a Mormon, and, you know, they’re the only church going to heaven. He’s not going to say that, but that’s what they say. And they can have sacred marriage. And see, “my faith,” and then, you know, [unclear] comes along and he just got saved, he got, you know, probably got saved so he could get elected by the Christians. That’s the way politicians do. I--I don’t know that’s the case, but, you know, it could be. You know, and he’s got the Catholic faith, and then you got [unclear], “my faith.” They’re all saying “my faith.” Well, where does the Bible say “my faith”?

It’s only mentioned twice in the Bible. Are you getting my drift? See, when I say “my faith,” what I’m saying is what I believe, and my opinions, they’re okay. Mr. Barnes’s faith can be different than mine, and so, and we got to accept everybody’s faith. That isn’t what the Bible says. Are you there? We don’t have a right to say “my faith,” and when you say “my faith,” you’re wrong. First place it’s used, James chapter 2:18: “Some say, you have faith, and I have works. Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you what”--my faith--how? By my works. See, what I do is going to show you what I’m persuaded in. How I live my life is going to show you what I really believe and I trust.

“You believe there is one God. Wow, you’re as good as the demons.” They believe there’s one God, and they tremble, because they know that God is going to put them in the lake of fire forever. Wow, you’re equal to the demons. You’re really doing good, man. Whoopee. Are you there? “Oh foolish man, faith without” what? Works “is dead.” Don’t say “my faith.” I will know your faith by how you act, how you speak, what you speak, what you do. That’s the first place that’s used.

chunks.section_question: Whose faith is “My faith” in Revelation 2, and why use the name of Jesus?
chunks.short_answer: He says in Revelation 2 Jesus says “You have not denied My faith,” and asks “whose faith? Who’s speaking there? Jesus Christ.” Jesus “was persuaded that He was God, that He was the Son of God, that He was the Savior of the world, that no man could get eternal life but through Him.” He says to use the name of Jesus because “God” is “a general word that can fit into anywhere.”
chunks.text:
Second place, before you condemn them to hell, my little thing: in Revelation 2:12, to the church of Pergamos, “I know your works.” Faith without works is dead. “You have not denied My faith.” Whose faith? Who’s speaking there? Jesus Christ. Only used two times. The first one is, my faith must be accompanied with works that Jesus said for me to do, or it’s dead. Here Jesus plainly says it is “My faith” that you should--

Have. What was Jesus persuaded in? Jesus was persuaded that He was God, that He was the Son of God, that He was the Savior of the world, that no man could get eternal life but through Him. Jesus was persuaded in the Bible faith, God’s faith. He was persuaded that He would do nothing without the will of the Father. Are you there, church? That’s the faith of Jesus Christ. Did Jesus sin? No. He said, “Yeah, well, He’s God.” Yes, but we should be pursuing the goal, shouldn’t we? Hallelujah. Even to martyrdom they would keep the faith of Christ, even if it cost them their life. If they were in a bad marriage, they wouldn’t give in to the bad spouse; they would keep the faith of Christ even if that spouse left them. If they had a rebellious son or daughter that wanted to do something else, they would keep the faith of Christ no matter what that child--

Did. So the real statement should not be “my faith,” but “the Bible.” If we believe the Bible, it says, yes, we should say, “Yes, I’m a Christian and I follow Jesus and His Word.” Why is it important to use the name of Jesus? Because today “God” is a general word that can fit into anywhere, but they hate Jesus. Even though He’s God, they don’t want Jesus, because of what Jesus stood for. They want the freedom to go to heaven and have eternal life without a lifestyle that represents Jesus Christ.

chunks.section_question: Can faith alone save a person, and what is “faith in your faith”? (James 2:14)
chunks.short_answer: He reads James 2:14 and says “in America faith is all you need.” He says “you don’t have the right faith” when you have faith in your faith, in a church or in a minister, and “the Bible never says to have faith in your faith.” We are to have the faith Jesus had, and “I may not be there yet, but I’m working on it.”
chunks.text:
Amen. “What does it profit,” James 2:14, “if someone says he has faith but does not have works?” What’s the profit? He says, you believe that you can go into the idol’s temple because idols are nothing, but what’s the profit? See, your works destroy your life. You get his argument. “Can faith save him?” And Paul is asking this question, and why? Because in America faith is all you need. The Baptist faith is all you need, you can live any way you want, but if you believe in Jesus, you’re going to heaven.

That’s the truth. In many Spirit-filled circles, if you believe in Christ, boy, and especially you [unclear] and speaking tongues, man, you are, you are in. Everything is focused on faith. The Catholics, if you believe in the Catholic church, you’re saved. The Mormons, if you believe in the Mormon church, you’re saved. And Paul, or James, is saying, can that faith save him? Can faith without works save anyone? That’s what James is saying. Am I talking to the right people? And these preachers in Protestant arenas that preach prosperity back it up with faith. Faith and prosperity is their message. And when you have faith in your faith, or faith in a church, or faith in a minister--

You don’t have the right faith. Now, I think this is liberating stuff. You’re looking at me like, “Man, this is deep.” Do you know how many people I know that have faith in their faith, and the Bible never says to have faith in your faith? We’re to have the faith that Jesus had, faith in God, faith in God’s Word, and be living and believing what He says. I may not be there yet, but I’m working on it. See, there’s a difference. One says, “I don’t see nothing wrong with this,” the other one says, “You know, I’m working on this. I’m working on--I haven’t got through this one yet, but I’m working on it, and God promised me that I will get through it, and I’ll get to another arena, and there’ll be another one.”

chunks.section_question: Is atheism a kind of faith?
chunks.short_answer: He says those who hold beliefs such as atheism “have faith in what they believe.” He says the Supreme Court declared atheism a religion “because they have a belief system. They believe there’s no God, and they have no evidence there is--that there isn’t one. That is faith, that is belief.”
chunks.text:
Amen. Atheists, evolutionists, humanists, homosexuals, the freethinkers, pro-choice, the liberals, Democrats, the Socialist Party, all have faith in what they believe. It’s totally faith. The evolutionists have no evidence; it’s totally faith. The socialists have evidence that socialism has not worked, and they still believe socialism will work. That’s a fact, and it’s never--

Worked. Pro-choice women could care the least about the baby; they just don’t want any strings attached to their loose lifestyle, and if they get pregnant they want to get rid of it so they can keep living loosely. That’s their faith. See, it doesn’t edify, it doesn’t profit anybody else. And all of these are 501(c)(3), just like our religious exemption. They say they’re nonprofit corporations, they’re religions, they’re a belief system. The Supreme Court declared atheism a religion because they have a belief system. They believe there’s no God, and they have no evidence there is--that there isn’t one. That is faith, that is belief.

faqs.question: What does it mean to ask “are we stronger than He”?
faqs.answer: He says it asks whether you use human understanding to “violate the direct commandments of God and provoke God to jealousy.” He asks, “Are you stronger than God? Have you become a God?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot partake of the Lord’s table and of the table of demons. Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?

faqs.question: Does Christian liberty mean anything goes?
faqs.answer: He says “all things are lawful for me, but all things” do not edify. He asks how his liberty in going into a pagan temple builds him up or the church “when I’m directly violating the Ten Commandments and other commandments.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: All things are lawful for me, but not all things are helpful; all things are lawful for me, but not all things edify.

faqs.question: What does he say a healthy church must be built on?
faqs.answer: He says you cannot build a healthy church “using your own opinions and your own beliefs. It must be Jesus, His truth, His words, and the apostles’ doctrine, who got their doctrine straight from Jesus.”

faqs.question: Why does he point to the Bible when people say they have a word from God?
faqs.answer: He asks, “why do I need to keep getting words of God from people when I have the Bible, which the Bible says is a more sure word of prophecy?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And so we have the prophetic word confirmed, which you do well to heed as a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts;

faqs.question: Does he say playing pool is a sin?
faqs.answer: No. He says “there’s nothing wrong with playing pool,” and that he has a pool table in his garage. He says in his youth it was called sin because the tables were in bars, “so instead of saying the atmosphere was wrong,” people called the game itself sin.

faqs.question: What does he say about being extreme?
faqs.answer: He says “the Bible says in Ecclesiastes, ‘do not be extreme in anything.’” He says “we need to watch out with being extreme. We need to be practical.”

faqs.question: Why did the apostles say to abstain from blood and things strangled?
faqs.answer: He says it is “because it’s related to Christ’s blood sacrifice for us. The blood had to be shed.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: that you abstain from things offered to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.

faqs.question: Does he say a person in a church with rituals cannot be a believer?
faqs.answer: No. He says it took God opening his understanding that “people can actually be a believer in Christ and be doing things in an erroneous way and still be a believer because they haven’t learned or come to the place yet where they can let go of the rituals and just embrace the truth.”

faqs.question: Does he say rich people are greedy?
faqs.answer: No. He asks, “does it mean because a person is rich that they’re greedy? No, the Bible doesn’t back up that at all.”

faqs.question: Is hatred listed among the works of the flesh?
faqs.answer: He reads it in the list and says hatred is when “you don’t like a certain race,” or women because they are women, or men because they are men, or rich because they are rich. He says it is a work of the flesh.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now the works of the flesh are evident, which are: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, contentions, jealousies, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambitions, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and the like; of which I tell you beforehand, just as I also told you in time past, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

faqs.question: What does he say about reading the horoscope?
faqs.answer: He asks, “do you read the horoscope every day?” and says “that’s an idol.” He says “before we start straightening everybody else out,” we need to straighten ourselves out.

faqs.question: How many times is “my faith” used in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says it is “only mentioned twice in the Bible”: the first place is James, where a person says “show me your faith without your works,” and the second is Jesus speaking to the church of Pergamos.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But someone will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

faqs.question: What does he say Jesus was persuaded of?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus “was persuaded that He was God, that He was the Son of God, that He was the Savior of the world, that no man could get eternal life but through Him,” and that He “would do nothing without the will of the Father.”

faqs.question: Why does he say it matters to use the name of Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says “God” is “a general word that can fit into anywhere, but they hate Jesus,” and they want “the freedom to go to heaven and have eternal life without a lifestyle that represents Jesus Christ.”
